sections.title: Test Coverage Gap Analysis
Overall Assessment
sections.content:
The test suite is solid for the **core quota/limiter logic** and **service layer**, but has significant gaps in the **controller layer** (especially `ConversionsController#download` and `BillingController#callback`), **auth flows** (`FirebaseTokenVerifier`, `FirebaseAuthController`), **payment service** (`PaystackService#verify_transaction`, billing callback), and several **edge cases** in well-tested units.

---

sections.title: Gap 1 — `User#from_omniauth` (entirely untested)
sections.content:
**File:** `app/models/user.rb:9`

Two paths: link OAuth to an existing email account, and create a brand-new OAuth user. Neither is covered. The "already confirmed?" branch on line 16 is an easy-to-miss edge case.

```ruby

sections.title: spec/models/user_spec.rb (add to existing file)
sections.content:
RSpec.describe User, type: :model do
  describe ".from_omniauth" do
    let(:auth) do
      double("OmniAuth::AuthHash",
        provider: "google_oauth2",
        uid:      "google-uid-123",
        info:     double(email: "test@example.com")
      )
    end

    it "links provider to an existing email account without creating a duplicate" do
      existing = create(:user, email: "test@example.com")
      result = User.from_omniauth(auth)
      expect(User.count).to eq(1)
      expect(result.uid).to eq("google-uid-123")
      expect(result.provider).to eq("google_oauth2")
    end

    it "auto-confirms an unconfirmed existing account after OAuth link" do
      existing = create(:user, email: "test@example.com", confirmed_at: nil)
      result = User.from_omniauth(auth)
      expect(result.confirmed_at).not_to be_nil
    end

    it "creates a new user when no matching email exists" do
      expect { User.from_omniauth(auth) }.to change(User, :count).by(1)
      user = User.last
      expect(user.email).to eq("test@example.com")
      expect(user.provider).to eq("google_oauth2")
      expect(user.confirmed_at).not_to be_nil  # auto-confirmed
    end

    it "is idempotent: calling twice with same auth returns the same record" do
      User.from_omniauth(auth)
      expect { User.from_omniauth(auth) }.not_to change(User, :count)
    end
  end

  describe "#conversion_limit_per_day" do
    it "returns 5 for free user" do
      expect(build(:user, plan: :free).conversion_limit_per_day).to eq(5)
    end

    it "returns 5 for inactive pro user" do
      expect(build(:user, plan: :pro, subscription_status: :inactive).conversion_limit_per_day).to eq(5)
    end

    it "returns infinity for active pro user" do
      expect(build(:user, plan: :pro, subscription_status: :active).conversion_limit_per_day).to eq(Float::INFINITY)
    end
  end
end
```

sections.content:

`validate_concurrency!` and the pro-user `:priority` queue assignment have no test coverage.

```ruby

describe "Concurrency limit" do
  it "blocks a user who already has too many in-flight jobs" do
    AppLimits::MAX_CONCURRENT_JOBS_PER_USER.times do
      Conversion.create!(user: free_user, tool_name: "Tools::CompressPdf", status: :processing)
    end

    runner = ToolRunner.new(free_user, "compress_pdf", [pdf_file])
    expect { runner.run! }.to raise_error(ToolRunner::LimitExceededError, /conversions still processing/)
  end
end

describe "Pro user gets priority queue" do
  it "enqueues on :priority queue for an active Pro user" do
    configured_job = instance_double(ActiveJob::ConfiguredJob)
    expect(ToolJob).to receive(:set).with(queue: :priority).and_return(configured_job)
    allow(configured_job).to receive(:perform_later)

    ToolRunner.new(pro_user, "compress_pdf", [pdf_file]).run!
  end
end

describe "INCONCLUSIVE_TYPES secondary check" do
  it "accepts a file whose bytes read as octet-stream when declared type + extension match" do
    path = Rails.root.join("tmp", "plain.pdf")
    File.binwrite(path, "some ambiguous content that reads as text/plain " * 5)
    ambiguous_file = Rack::Test::UploadedFile.new(path, "application/pdf")

    # Marcel may detect this as text/plain (inconclusive) — declared type + .pdf ext should pass
    allow(Marcel::MimeType).to receive(:for).and_return("text/plain")
    allow(ToolJob).to receive(:set).and_return(double(perform_later: true))

    expect { ToolRunner.new(free_user, "compress_pdf", [ambiguous_file]).run! }.not_to raise_error
  end
end
```

sections.title: Gap 4 — `BillingController#callback` (entirely untested)
sections.content:
**File:** `app/controllers/billing_controller.rb:25-51`

This is the most critical gap from a business perspective — the callback that upgrades users to Pro after a successful payment has zero test coverage.

```ruby

sections.title: spec/requests/billing_spec.rb (add to existing file)
sections.content:
describe "GET /billing/callback" do
  let(:reference) { "txn_ref_abc123" }

  it "upgrades user to Pro when Paystack confirms success" do
    sign_in user
    paystack_data = {
      "status" => "success",
      "customer" => { "customer_code" => "CUS_test" },
      "plan_object" => { "subscription_code" => "SUB_test" }
    }
    allow_any_instance_of(PaystackService).to receive(:verify_transaction).and_return(paystack_data)

    get callback_billing_path, params: { trxref: reference }

    user.reload
    expect(user.plan).to eq("pro")
    expect(user.subscription_status).to eq("active")
    expect(user.paystack_customer_code).to eq("CUS_test")
    expect(response).to have_http_status(:ok)
  end

  it "does not double-track analytics when user is already active" do
    sign_in user
    user.update!(plan: :pro, subscription_status: :active)
    allow_any_instance_of(PaystackService).to receive(:verify_transaction)
      .and_return({ "status" => "success", "customer" => {}, "plan_object" => {} })

    expect(Analytics).not_to receive(:track).with(:subscription_activated, anything)
    get callback_billing_path, params: { trxref: reference }
  end

  it "renders the page without error when reference is missing" do
    sign_in user
    get callback_billing_path  # no trxref param
    expect(response).to have_http_status(:ok)
    expect(user.reload.plan).to eq("free")  # unchanged
  end

  it "renders the page without error when Paystack verify returns false" do
    sign_in user
    allow_any_instance_of(PaystackService).to receive(:verify_transaction).and_return(false)
    get callback_billing_path, params: { trxref: reference }
    expect(response).to have_http_status(:ok)
    expect(user.reload.plan).to eq("free")
  end
end
```

sections.title: Gap 6 — `FirebaseTokenVerifier` (entirely untested)
sections.content:
**File:** `app/services/firebase_token_verifier.rb`

The entire Firebase JWT verification flow — including cert fetch, caching, signature verification, and failure modes — has no tests.

```ruby

sections.title: spec/services/firebase_token_verifier_spec.rb (new file)
sections.content:
require 'rails_helper'

RSpec.describe FirebaseTokenVerifier do
  let(:project_id) { "test-project" }

  before { stub_const("ENV", ENV.to_h.merge("FIREBASE_PROJECT_ID" => project_id)) }

  describe ".verify" do
    it "returns nil when the token is malformed/unparseable" do
      expect(FirebaseTokenVerifier.verify("not.a.jwt")).to be_nil
    end

    it "returns nil when the kid is not in Google's certificate list" do
      token = JWT.encode({ "sub" => "uid123" }, nil, "none")
      allow(Rails.cache).to receive(:fetch).and_return({ "other_kid" => "cert" })
      allow(JWT).to receive(:decode).with(token, nil, false).and_return([{}, { "kid" => "missing_kid" }])
      expect(FirebaseTokenVerifier.verify(token)).to be_nil
    end

    it "returns nil when cert fetch fails (network error)" do
      stub_request(:get, FirebaseTokenVerifier::CERT_URL).to_timeout
      allow(Rails.cache).to receive(:fetch).and_yield  # bypass cache
      valid_token = JWT.encode({}, nil, "none")  # forces cert fetch path
      expect(FirebaseTokenVerifier.verify(valid_token)).to be_nil
    end

    it "returns the decoded payload on a valid RS256-signed token" do
      # Use a real RSA key pair to sign a token that passes all checks.
      key = OpenSSL::PKey::RSA.generate(2048)
      cert = OpenSSL::X509::Certificate.new.tap do |c|
        c.public_key = key.public_key
        c.sign(key, OpenSSL::Digest::SHA256.new)
      end
      kid = "valid_kid"
      payload = {
        "sub" => "uid123", "email" => "u@test.com",
        "aud" => project_id,
        "iss" => "https://securetoken.google.com/#{project_id}",
        "exp" => (Time.current + 1.hour).to_i,
        "iat" => Time.current.to_i
      }
      token = JWT.encode(payload, key, "RS256", { "kid" => kid })
      allow(Rails.cache).to receive(:fetch).and_return({ kid => cert.to_pem })

      result = FirebaseTokenVerifier.verify(token)
      expect(result["email"]).to eq("u@test.com")
    end
  end
end
```

```ruby
require 'rails_helper'

RSpec.describe PaystackService do
  before do
    stub_const("ENV", ENV.to_h.merge(

    let(:reference) { "txn_123" }

        .to_return(status: 200, body: {

    it "returns false (does not raise) on network error" do
      stub_request(:get, /paystack.co\/transaction\/verify/).to_timeout

  describe "ConfigurationError" do
    it "raises ConfigurationError for initialize_subscription when credentials missing" do
```

sections.title: Gap 9 — `Tools::BaseTool` timeout + empty output (untested paths)
sections.content:
**File:** `app/services/tools/base_tool.rb:38-52, 107-115`

The `Timeout::Error` rescue branch and the `attach_output` small-file guard are untested.

```ruby

sections.title: spec/services/tools/base_tool_spec.rb (add to existing file)
sections.content:
class TimeoutTool < Tools::BaseTool
  protected
  def process(input_paths)
    raise Timeout::Error
  end
end

class TinyOutputTool < Tools::BaseTool
  protected
  def process(input_paths)
    path = tmp_path("tiny.pdf")
    File.write(path, "x")  # 1 byte — below the 100-byte guard
    path
  end
end

describe "timeout handling" do
  it "marks failed, refunds quota, and does NOT re-raise" do
    conv = Conversion.create!(user: user, tool_name: "TimeoutTool", status: :pending, usage_counted: true)
    conv.input_files.attach(file)
    user.update!(conversions_count: 2)

    expect { TimeoutTool.new(conv).call }.not_to raise_error

    expect(conv.reload.status).to eq("failed")
    expect(conv.error_message).to include("timed out")
    expect(user.reload.conversions_count).to eq(1)  # refunded
  end
end

describe "empty/corrupt output guard" do
  it "raises ExecutionError (permanent) when output is < 100 bytes" do
    conv = Conversion.create!(user: user, tool_name: "TinyOutputTool", status: :pending)
    conv.input_files.attach(file)

    expect { TinyOutputTool.new(conv).call }.not_to raise_error
    expect(conv.reload.status).to eq("failed")
    expect(conv.error_message).to include("empty or corrupt")
  end
end
```

```ruby
describe "retry exhaustion callback" do
  it "marks failed and refunds quota after all retries are exhausted" do
    user.update!(conversions_count: 3)
    conversion = Conversion.create!(user: user, tool_name: "Tools::CompressPdf",
                                    status: :processing, usage_counted: true)

    # Simulate what SolidQueue calls when retries are exhausted
    error = StandardError.new("persistent failure")
    job = ToolJob.new
    job.arguments = [conversion.id]  # simulate the job argument
    ToolJob.rescue_handlers
           .find { |h, _| h == "StandardError" }
           &.last&.call(job, error)

    expect(conversion.reload.status).to eq("failed")
    expect(conversion.reload.error_message).to include("several attempts")
    expect(user.reload.conversions_count).to eq(2)
  end
end
```

The highest-value work is P1: `BillingController#callback` and `ConversionsController#download` together cover the money path and the file delivery path — two places where bugs are costly and currently invisible to the test suite.

require 'rails_helper'

RSpec.describe FirebaseTokenVerifier do
  let(:project_id) { "test-project" }

  before { stub_const("ENV", ENV.to_h.merge("FIREBASE_PROJECT_ID" => project_id)) }

  describe ".verify" do
    it "returns nil when the token is malformed/unparseable" do
      expect(FirebaseTokenVerifier.verify("not.a.jwt")).to be_nil
    end

    it "returns nil when the kid is not in Google's certificate list" do
      token = JWT.encode({ "sub" => "uid123" }, nil, "none")
      allow(Rails.cache).to receive(:fetch).and_return({ "other_kid" => "cert" })
      allow(JWT).to receive(:decode).with(token, nil, false).and_return([{}, { "kid" => "missing_kid" }])
      expect(FirebaseTokenVerifier.verify(token)).to be_nil
    end

    it "returns nil when cert fetch fails (network error)" do
      stub_request(:get, FirebaseTokenVerifier::CERT_URL).to_timeout
      allow(Rails.cache).to receive(:fetch).and_yield  # bypass cache
      valid_token = JWT.encode({}, nil, "none")  # forces cert fetch path
      expect(FirebaseTokenVerifier.verify(valid_token)).to be_nil
    end

    it "returns the decoded payload on a valid RS256-signed token" do
      # Use a real RSA key pair to sign a token that passes all checks.
      key = OpenSSL::PKey::RSA.generate(2048)
      cert = OpenSSL::X509::Certificate.new.tap do |c|
        c.public_key = key.public_key
        c.sign(key, OpenSSL::Digest::SHA256.new)
      end
      kid = "valid_kid"
      payload = {
        "sub" => "uid123", "email" => "u@test.com",
        "aud" => project_id,
        "iss" => "https://securetoken.google.com/#{project_id}",
        "exp" => (Time.current + 1.hour).to_i,
        "iat" => Time.current.to_i
      }
      token = JWT.encode(payload, key, "RS256", { "kid" => kid })
      allow(Rails.cache).to receive(:fetch).and_return({ kid => cert.to_pem })

      result = FirebaseTokenVerifier.verify(token)
      expect(result["email"]).to eq("u@test.com")
    end
  end
end
